A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 31-page versions of the same FEAT paper. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original free-energy estimation experiments on Gaussian mixtures, molecular systems, and lattice field theory, plus runtime, robustness, and transferability results in Appendix E.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results, including the main-text comparisons and the additional analyses in Appendix E.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same stochastic-interpolant training, boundary correction, forward-backward estimator, variance minimization, and one-sided FEAT procedure. No algorithm or architecture changes are documented.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Gaussian mixtures, Lennard-Jones systems, alanine dipeptide tasks, lattice field theory, alanine tetrapeptide, Chignolin, and transferable GMM scenarios. The new condensed-phase citation does not add experiments to this paper.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain targeted FEP with flow matching, Neural TI with and without preconditioning, and MBAR reference values. Comparator membership in the appendix analyses also remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Table 8 and Appendix F preserve the same sampling procedures, preprocessing, training budgets, model sizes, evaluation sample counts, discretization settings, and baseline protocols.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same estimator-training dynamics, umbrella-sampling demonstration, runtime analysis, sample-size and discretization sensitivity tests, and transferability analysis in Figure 2, Figures 3–4, and Appendix E.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains mean and standard deviation reporting across three runs with different seeds. Appendix E.3 retains its three-run uncertainty reporting; no run-count, seed, or statistical-reporting changes are documented.

E6.justification: The numerical entries in Tables 1–7 and the findings displayed in Figures 1–4 are unchanged. For example, Table 3 retains FEAT estimates of 109.91 ± 2.55 for ALA-4 and 320.02 ± 0.70 for Chignolin.

T1.justification: The mathematical statements, assumptions, equations, and appendix proofs are unchanged. References to 'Theorem' are corrected to the existing Corollary 3.1 and Propositions 3.2–3.3; the Section 5 overlap edit revises an informal interpretation rather than a formal definition or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and central conclusion retain the same contributions: unifying equilibrium and non-equilibrium estimation, consistent minimum-variance estimators, variational bounds, and practical computational advantages.

C2.justification: Section 5 removes the identification of overlap with 'mutual information' while retaining the data-processing argument, and makes the bias-variance interpretation more tentative. It replaces the explicit call for reliability diagnostics with a condensed-phase evaluation citation and adds extending computational-complexity analysis as future work.

D1.justification: The implementation link, Algorithm 1, architecture descriptions, hyperparameters, data-processing instructions, baseline implementation details, and single 80 GB NVIDIA H100 disclosure remain unchanged. Appendix-reference wording changes add no reproducibility information.

R1.justification: v3 adds Schebek et al. (2025) on evaluating generative free-energy estimation in condensed matter and Guo et al. (2025) on normalizing-constant estimation complexity. These contextualize limitations and future work without substantially changing the paper's novelty positioning.

P1.justification: v3 edits the equal-contribution footnote, standardizes appendix references, corrects theorem-type labels throughout the text and appendix contents, and briefly revises Section 5. The section order and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Minor spacing and text reflow shift Tables 2–3 and surrounding text within their pages and alter bibliography page breaks. The figures, table structures, captions, and main-text versus appendix placement are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 corrects inconsistent theorem labels, clarifies appendix references, and modestly improves the research context of Section 5. Although the explicit diagnostic-development sentence is dropped, the high-variance warning remains. These are limited clarity and contextual gains; the method, proofs, and experimental evidence are unchanged.
